To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The new global fit of the latest parity violating electron scattering (PVES) data on the weak neutral current (WNC) couplings to light quarks is in excellent agreement with the standard model (SM) predictions, 2) This result improves the lower limit on the scale of physics beyond the SM (B-SM) by a factor of 2.5, 3) The new result is consistent with the atomic PV (APV) measurements of the WNC

the new global analysis of parity-violating electron-scattering data has improved our knowledge of the weak-neutral current lepton-quark couplings, and that this new result, together with the atomic parity-violation data, has improved the lower-bound on new physics by approximately a factor of 2.
the weak charges of the u- and d-quarks are measured to be quark weak charge = (− 0.37 ± 0.17) e, quark weak charge (− 0. 35 ± 0.18) e, where e is the unit of charge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the precise determination of the weak charges (or couplings) of the quarks, which is a key test of the electroweak theory and a probe of new physics.
the precise measurement of the weak neutral currents in low-energy interactions of leptons with hadrons.
precision measurements of the weak neutral current (WNC) interaction of quarks and the determination of the weak charge of the proton.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this new result, together with the earlier measurements, provides a very strong test of the standard electroweak theory and a significant improvement in constraining new physics beyond it.
the standard model of electroweak interactions, with three generations of quarks and leptons, is a very good description of nature at the present time.
the Standard Model (SM) is a consistent and well-tested theory of electroweak interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have improved our knowledge on the weak neutral-current couplings of quarks at low energies by more than a factor of two, and have placed a new lower-bound on the energy scale of new physics at approximately 1 Tev.
the weak neutral-current couplings are well determined, and the standard model of electroweak interactions remains valid at the low energy scale.
the standard model of particle physics has been tested at a precision that is comparable to the precision of the standard model itself.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the weak charges of the quarks are now known with sufficient precision that the weak interactions of quarks can be compared with the weak interactions of leptons, and that the standard model is now being tested by precision measurements of the quark weak charges.
precision measurements in atomic and nuclear physics can be a powerful complement to high-energy physics in the search for new physics beyond the standard-model.
the weak charges of the light quarks are now known at the percent level and that these quantities are sensitive probes of new physics at the TeV scale.
